title: Exchanging Only What I'd Decided
description:
{name} once exchanged 'only the amount decided' in chips at the casino.

That line of restraint comes back sometimes.

Today the temptation of one big bet crosses the mind.

choices.text: Setting a line — was the only way out
choices.result_text:
The one thing that kept reason at the table was the line set in advance.

That line kept {name} out of the abyss.
Only what you can afford to lose — that was the survivor's rule.

choices.text: Now I know — better not to cross even that line
choices.result_text:
Setting a line is good, but not stepping in at all was safer.

{name} knows the nature of that temptation.
₩3 billion was elsewhere, not at the gambling table.

title: Loading Up on Chips
description:
{name} once loaded up on casino chips, thinking 'running short kills the mood.'

They know the danger of that choice now.

A similar situation comes to mind today.

choices.text: That was risky — now I set tight limits
choices.result_text:
Plenty of chips led straight to plenty of losses.

{name} learned the more chips in front of you, the harder to quit.
Needing an empty pocket to walk away was gambling's cruel truth.

choices.text: Better yet — don't sit at that table at all
choices.result_text:
It wasn't about how many chips to exchange.

{name} knows sitting at that table is itself the risk.
The best restraint was not entering the room of temptation.

title: Losing Track of Time
description:
In a clockless casino, {name} repeated 'just one more game' and lost track of time.

That dazed stretch comes back sometimes.

Today the 'just once more' temptation returns.

choices.text: The time to quit — isn't after winning
choices.result_text:
'I'll stop when I win' was a trap. Winning makes you want more.

{name} learned to quit by a set time.
Stopping by the clock, not the result — that was the only rule that worked.

choices.text: That dazed time scared me — never again
choices.result_text:
Losing the sense of time chilled {name}.

They learned in the body that addiction begins like that.
As long as they remember that chill, they won't linger long in that room again.

title: Choosing the Last Train
description:
When the casino offered a free night's stay, {name} declined — 'I'll catch the last train home.'

That refusal comes back sometimes.

Today they face another temptation disguised as kindness.

choices.text: Free favors — always have a price
choices.result_text:
A free night was meant to keep you longer.

{name} read the favor's intent.
That last-train night saved them from a bigger loss.

choices.text: Leaving that place — was the hardest victory
choices.result_text:
The hardest thing in gambling is leaving.

Declining the favor and catching the last train, {name} truly won.
Only those who can leave that place win elsewhere.

title: Accepting the Free Night
description:
When the casino offered a free night's stay, {name} accepted — 'just one night, then.'

They know how that night went.

Today a similar temptation beckons.

choices.text: I learned then — free favors were bait
choices.result_text:
The night they stayed longer, they lost more.

{name} learned the casino's favors were strategy, not kindness.
The real price of what looks free is always billed later.

choices.text: Now — even when offered, I take the last train
choices.result_text:
That regret changed {name}.

Now, however good the offer, they leave at the set time.
Restraint learned from a mistake prevented the same mistake.

title: That Could Be My Future, I Said
description:
Watching someone go all-in and collapse at the holdem table, {name} left, thinking 'that could be my future.'

That warning comes back sometimes.

Today there's a temptation as the pot grows.

choices.text: From another's fall — I learned my brake
choices.result_text:
You can learn from another's collapse without collapsing yourself.

That scene became the brake in {name}'s mind.
A warning only matters if it comes before it's too late.

choices.text: Leaving that seat — was the real skill
choices.result_text:
Leaving while winning is the hardest thing.

{name} did that hard thing.
More than reading hands well, knowing when to leave was the greater skill.

title: Using That Instinct at Work
description:
{name} once decided to use the instincts honed in holdem for work and investing, not gambling. 'Cut down on the table.'

That pivot comes back sometimes.

Today they consider where to apply that instinct.

choices.text: Use the sense for odds and bets — in investing
choices.result_text:
Calculating expected value, avoiding overbetting, knowing when to cut losses.

That holdem instinct shone in investing.
The same ability, applied differently, parted lives.

choices.text: Use the eye for risk — in business judgment
choices.result_text:
The gambling sense for risk was, in fact, useful in every decision.

{name} applied that eye to life's judgments, not gambling.
An ability that nearly became addiction turned into an asset.

title: Hyung, Let's Leave Together Today
description:
At the racetrack, {name} extended a hand to a tip-sheet seller who couldn't pull himself out — 'Hyung, let's leave together today' — and they left.

That moment of reaching out comes back sometimes.

That hyung came to mind today.

choices.text: Pulling someone out — saved me too
choices.result_text:
Trying to pull another out, {name} stepped out of that line themselves.

Gambling is a swamp you fall into and can't leave alone, but a hand makes it different.
The hand offered that day saved them both.

choices.text: I wonder how that hyung is — I hope he's okay
choices.result_text:
Word stopped after they left together.

{name} hoped that hyung had escaped that line for good.
A compassion known only to those who've seen the same swamp lingered in a corner of the heart.

title: Leaving the Last Line
description:
In the final race, {name} stepped out of the line chasing a comeback — 'I know how this line ends.'

That moment of leaving comes back sometimes.

Today there's the 'one last time' temptation.

choices.text: That line's end — was always a deeper pit
choices.result_text:
The last bet chasing a comeback was usually the start of a bigger loss.

{name} knows where that line ends.
Knowing how to leave was what everyone in that line couldn't do.

choices.text: I learned to let losses stay losses
choices.result_text:
The urge to recoup ruins people.

{name} learned to accept the loss and walk away.
The moment they let go of getting even, their foot finally came free of the swamp.

title: Betting Big Because It Was the Last
description:
In the final race, {name} bet big, calling it 'a chance to recoup.'

They know that bet's result.

Today the temptation to 'recoup in one shot' returns.

choices.text: I learned then — comeback bets were always a deeper hole
choices.result_text:
That big 'last' bet only widened the hole.

{name} learned to the bone that the recoup temptation is the most dangerous.
The urge to fill it in one shot ultimately collapsed everything.

choices.text: That loss — became the reason I quit gambling
choices.result_text:
The day of the big loss, paradoxically, made {name} stop.

Some people have to see the bottom before they can climb.
That bet was the worst, but it also became a turning point.

title: Going to That Blind Date
description:
{name} once went to a blind date, 'curious what kind of person they'd be.'

That meeting comes back sometimes.

Today came a moment of wondering whether to meet someone.

choices.text: Staying open to meeting — is part of life too
choices.result_text:
Close yourself to people while absorbed in a goal, and even arriving leaves an empty side.

{name} decided not to lose an open heart toward meeting.
Connection comes from outside the planner.

choices.text: For now — the goal comes before people
choices.result_text:
No room to say yes to every meeting.

{name} decided to focus on their path for now.
When the time comes, the person you're meant to meet, you'll meet — no searching needed.

title: Expressing How I Felt
description:
{name} once expressed feelings to a coworker.

That courage — or recklessness — comes back sometimes.

Today came another moment of hesitating whether to express feelings.

choices.text: No regret expressing it — better than burying it
choices.result_text:
Whatever the result, saying it beat regret.

Buried feelings end up as lingering attachment.
{name} felt a self who can express beats a self who shuts it away.

choices.text: Should've picked the time and place — learn discretion
choices.result_text:
Between people working in the same space, expression carries weight.

{name} learned the balance between honesty and discretion.
Saying how you feel and knowing when to say it were different skills.

title: Asking to Meet Again
description:
{name} once replied 'let's meet' to an ex's message.

That meeting comes back sometimes.

Today thoughts of a past connection drift by.

choices.text: Glad I met them — I needed closure
choices.result_text:
What they learned by meeting again was that the connection had truly passed.

Some knots only come undone face to face.
{name} could lay the lingering feelings to rest through that meeting.

choices.text: The past is the past — look forward
choices.result_text:
Spend too long looking back and you lose the strength to go forward.

{name} made that meeting the last, and set their gaze ahead.
Recall the past sometimes, but don't live there.

title: Trying a Dating App
description:
{name} once tried a dating app.

That attempt comes back sometimes.

Today, between loneliness and the wish to connect, that time came to mind.

choices.text: The attempt itself — was proof I wasn't closed off
choices.result_text:
Whatever the result, reaching for connection mattered.

{name} acknowledged the self who reached out not to be isolated.
Even amid the busyness, not closing the door toward people.

choices.text: Over apps — I'll wait for a natural connection
choices.result_text:
A connection that comes in the flow felt easier than one anxiously sought.

{name} deleted the app and decided to focus on their life for now.
Connection is needed, but it didn't have to be forced.
